papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies SLCO1B3 as a prognostic marker and functional oncogenic driver in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a leading cause of cancer mortality with limited prognostic biomarkers. Given the role of metabolic reprogramming in tumor progression, this study investigated the clinical relevance and biological function of the lipid metabolism-associated transporter SLCO1B3 in HNSCC.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to show that the lipid metabolism transporter SLCO1B3 is associated with prognosis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and appears to functionally promote tumor growth. The authors propose SLCO1B3 as both a prognostic biomarker and a potential oncogenic driver in HNSCC.

papers.title: Mid-zone hepatocytes trade proliferation for survival via Atf4-Chop axis in early acute liver injury.
papers.abstract: Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Using a mouse model of acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, we show that hepatocytes undergo transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. Although spatial transcriptomics (ST) alone could not independently confirm zonal proliferative restraint, ST analysis identified a unique mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis. By integrating Cut&Run
papers.summary: Using a mouse model of acetaminophen-induced liver injury, the authors show that hepatocytes in the mid-zone of the liver lobule transiently suppress proliferation early after injury, matching the zonal pattern of APAP metabolism. Spatial transcriptomics revealed a mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis, suggesting these cells prioritize survival over proliferation during the early adaptive phase.

papers.title: Bacteria inside kidney tumors associate with myeloid inflammation and disease progression: A TRACERx Renal study.
papers.abstract: Intratumoral bacteria are increasingly recognized as active contributors to neutrophil-driven inflammation and disease progression in solid tumors. Yet, in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), where myeloid inflammation is a key feature of aggressive disease, live bacterial presence, their intratumoral distribution, and interaction with the tumor microenvironment remain unexplored.
papers.summary: This study investigates live bacteria within clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) tumors, examining their distribution and interaction with the tumor microenvironment. The authors link intratumoral bacterial presence to myeloid inflammation and disease progression, suggesting bacteria may actively contribute to aggressive ccRCC.

papers.title: Standardizing spatial transcriptomic analysis for infectious diseases with STID.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomic studies of infectious diseases still rely on fragmented data analysis processes. Here, we developed STID (spatial transcriptomics toolkit for infectious diseases), a standardized framework for spatial transcriptomic analysis of infectious diseases that leverages the Seurat ecosystem and incorporates Python-based modules. STID provides an extensible infection-specific data structure and supports a full suite of analyses, such as pathogen background correction, infection-associated spot and niche identification, single-sample niche characterization, and multi-sample compar
papers.summary: STID is a standardized software framework for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data from infectious disease studies. It builds on the Seurat ecosystem with Python modules and provides an extensible infection-specific data structure, supporting analyses such as pathogen background correction, infection-associated spot and niche identification, and multi-sample comparisons. The toolkit aims to replace fragmented analysis workflows with a unified, reproducible pipeline.

papers.title: Advances in Single-Cell and Spatial Omics for Glioblastoma Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma is the most aggressive and fatal primary malignant brain tumour in adults, characterised by extensive intra-tumour heterogeneity, diffuse infiltration into surrounding brain tissue. Despite advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, patient prognosis remains poor, underscoring the critical need for improved biological insight to guide precision medicine potential strategies. Although traditional bulk genomic and transcriptomic analyses have made a substantial contribution to understanding glioblastoma pathophysiology, such average molecular signals across cell population
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell and spatial omics technologies are being applied to glioblastoma, the most aggressive adult brain tumor. These methods reveal the extensive cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization within tumors that bulk genomic and transcriptomic approaches miss, offering new avenues for precision medicine strategies.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics with computational pathology to identify a stem-like epithelial population in bladder cancer marked by C11orf24. This population is associated with remodeling of the tumor microenvironment and immune evasion, suggesting a role in disease progression and therapeutic resistance.

papers.title: A multi-omics study integrating single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and mendelian randomization unveil the implication of TRDMT1 expression in T cells on the immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: m5C, an important RNA modification, is closely associated with breast cancer; however, their causal relationship is unknown. We examined the relationship between m5C regulation and breast cancer. Genome-wide association study breast cancer data and expression quantitative trait loci of m5C regulatory factor genes in blood were collected. We explored the causal relationship among m5C regulatory genes, breast cancer susceptibility, and prognosis through Mendelian randomization. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells of patients with breast cancer and healthy cont
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and Mendelian randomization to investigate how m5C RNA modification regulators, particularly TRDMT1, influence breast cancer susceptibility, prognosis, and immunotherapy response. The authors identify TRDMT1 expression in T cells as a potential causal factor affecting immunotherapeutic outcomes, linking m5C regulation to breast cancer biology through a multi-omics framework.

papers.title: Peritoneal dialysis induces hepatic metabolic stress as an instigator for systemic inflammation.
papers.abstract: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is a lifesaving therapy in patients with kidney failure, but results in daily intraperitoneal glucose administration corresponding to 50% of the recommended energy intake, most of which enters the portal circulation. As the impact of this glucose exposure on liver and metabolic health remains unclear, we explored hepatic and systemic metabolic effects of PD.
papers.summary: This study investigates how peritoneal dialysis (PD), which delivers large amounts of glucose into the portal circulation, affects liver metabolism and systemic inflammation. The authors find that PD induces hepatic metabolic stress, which appears to act as an instigator for systemic inflammation. This highlights a potential metabolic mechanism linking PD therapy to inflammatory complications in kidney failure patients.

papers.title: Oxidative Stress Potentiates a STAT1-APOL1 Feedforward Loop and Governs Disease Severity in APOL1-Mediated Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) risk variants (G1 and G2) confer immunity against Trypanosoma infection but markedly increase susceptibility to progressive kidney disease. However, only a subset of biallelic risk-variant carriers develops disease progression, distinct from murine models. Here, we evaluated molecular drivers of progressive kidney disease using a model that reflected the low human disease penetrance.
papers.summary: This study investigates why only some people carrying APOL1 risk variants develop progressive kidney disease, using a model that mimics the low disease penetrance seen in humans. The authors identify a STAT1-APOL1 feedforward loop that is potentiated by oxidative stress and governs disease severity, suggesting that oxidative stress drives the loop to determine which carriers progress.

papers.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised
papers.summary: CDState is a computational method that deconvolves bulk tumor RNA sequencing data to resolve intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity into distinct malignant cell states without requiring supervised reference data. This enables scalable characterization of cell-state diversity across large cancer cohorts where single-cell sequencing is impractical.

papers.title: CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) play important roles in various biological processes, primarily via regulating gene expression at multiple levels. Nevertheless, compared to protein-coding genes, ncRNAs are relatively understudied. They are characterized by low expression, large variation, and more dynamic expression across different tissues and cell types, which creates unique challenges in differential expression (DE) analysis. Methods: We propose the CQRM, an adaptive multi-quantile testing framework for ncRNA count data that incorporates jittering to accommodate discrete cou
papers.summary: The authors propose CQRM, a composite quantile regression framework for differential expression analysis of non-coding RNA count data. The method uses jittering to handle discrete counts and adaptively combines multiple quantile levels, addressing the low expression and high variability characteristic of ncRNAs. This provides an alternative to standard mean-based DE methods for this challenging data type.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, overcoming a major technical barrier to studying these cells in vivo. They then profiled the transcriptome of these MGCs, providing the first gene expression signature for these hemophagocytic, heavily parasitized cells in visceral leishmaniasis. This work offers a foundation for understanding how MGCs may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to build a compact risk score predicting pulmonary metastasis or relapse in osteosarcoma, centered on a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated program. The work links a specific gene signature to reduced immune activity and identifies single-cell programs associated with metastatic risk, offering a potential prognostic tool for this aggressive bone cancer.

papers.title: Scalable localization of clustering instability for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Standard spatial transcriptomics workflows rely on clustering methods to define regions of interest for down-stream analyses, such as differential expression and pathway enrichment. Although researchers are presented with a single partition, most clustering methods are stochastic, meaning their output depends on random algorithmic choices, typically controlled by a seed; thus, repeating the analysis changing only the seed can yield a different result. Spatial transcriptomics data may be especially sensitive to algorithmic perturbations due to high dimensionality, sparsity, and mixed expression
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a method to identify which spatial regions in transcriptomics data are unstable across different random seeds of clustering algorithms. By localizing instability, it helps researchers distinguish robust tissue domains from those that are artifacts of algorithmic randomness, improving downstream analyses like differential expression.

papers.title: SPP1⁺ macrophage-derived WNT5A contributes to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the stromal-immune circuits that coordinate matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the stromal-immune interactions associated with LUAD progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade.
papers.summary: This study identifies a stromal-immune circuit in lung adenocarcinoma in which SPP1⁺ macrophages secrete WNT5A to drive the differentiation and matrix-remodeling activity of MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblasts (myCAFs). This macrophage–fibroblast axis is associated with tumor progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade, suggesting it as a potential therapeutic target or biomarker for immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Cell-Cell Communication Patterns in Alzheimer's Disease Differ by Cortical Layer.
papers.abstract: Existing cell-cell communication (CCC) studies of Alzheimer's disease dementia (ADD) using cortical snRNAseq data do not account for the distinct cell-type and gene-expression profiles within cortical layers. Cortical-layer-aware CCC analysis may clarify biological mechanisms associated with ADD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint argues that existing cell-cell communication analyses of Alzheimer's disease using cortical snRNA-seq data ignore the distinct cellular and transcriptional profiles of individual cortical layers. The authors propose a cortical-layer-aware framework for CCC analysis, which they suggest may clarify mechanisms underlying Alzheimer's disease dementia and mild cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Native, Memory-Bounded Conversion of Mass Spectrometry Imaging Data into the SpatialData Ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) is now a routine modality for spatial molecular profiling and is increasingly combined with histology, multiplexed imaging, and spatial transcriptomics to build richer descriptions of tissue than any single technique can provide. The conceptual case for this multimodal paradigm was settled a decade ago, but the data infrastructure needed to operationalize it at scale has not kept up. Vendor binaries and the imzML exchange format keep MSI outside the OME-NGFF, Zarr, and SpatialData stacks on which the rest of spatial omics has converged, leaving each new experime
papers.journal: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry
papers.summary: This paper presents a tool for converting mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data into the SpatialData ecosystem, which is the standard data infrastructure used by other spatial omics modalities. The conversion works natively and with bounded memory, enabling MSI data to be integrated with histology, multiplexed imaging, and spatial transcriptomics in a unified framework. This addresses a key infrastructure gap that has kept MSI outside the OME-NGFF, Zarr, and SpatialData stacks.

papers.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic technologies generate large-scale gene expression datasets for functional module discovery. However, technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and compromise module detection. Noise-tolerant methods are therefore needed to recover meaningful biclusters.
papers.summary: The authors present NoiBic, a biclustering algorithm designed to tolerate noise in high-throughput gene expression data. The method aims to recover coherent gene-sample modules that would otherwise be obscured by technical and biological noise, improving functional module discovery from transcriptomic datasets.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing single-cell expression through the lens of topic modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP introduces a topic-modeling approach to recover gene-expression programs from single-cell RNA-seq data without forcing each gene into a single program, preserving the many-to-many structure of gene regulation. Unlike trajectory-based methods that assign genes to one program, it allows genes and cells to participate in multiple co-regulated modules simultaneously. This provides a more faithful representation of the overlapping programs that cells run concurrently.

papers.title: Dermatopathology 2030: Navigating the Digital, Computational and Molecular Convergence for Precision Diagnostics-Originated from a Round Table Discussion at A 66, Basel.
papers.abstract: Background: Traditional dermatopathology relies on analog, qualitative pattern recognition, which encounters critical limitations when facing diagnostic "gray zones" and ambiguous tumor proliferations. Objectives: This paper synthesizes a comprehensive framework integrating Whole Slide Imaging (WSI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and multi-omics to evaluate how this structural convergence redesigns diagnostic risk and safety ecosystems toward 2030. Methods: We analyze the conceptual shift from individual microscope-based observation to multiple data integration. We integrate recent algorithmic
papers.summary: This perspective piece synthesizes a roundtable discussion on how dermatopathology is moving from analog microscope-based diagnosis toward an integrated digital workflow combining whole-slide imaging, artificial intelligence, and multi-omics. The authors argue that this convergence can help resolve diagnostic gray zones and ambiguous tumor proliferations, and they outline a framework for redesigning diagnostic risk and safety systems through 2030.

papers.title: Cell-Cell Communication in Embryonic Kidney Development: Insights from Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Embryonic kidney morphogenesis depends on the coordinated communication among ureteric epithelium, nephron progenitors, stroma, endothelium and differentiating nephrons. Classical studies established central roles for glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) signaling through the RET proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase (RET), WNT-family signaling, fibroblast growth factor (FGF), bone morphogenetic protein (BMP), Notch, Hedgehog, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) pathways, but pathway-centered models do not fully explain why simila
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are reshaping our understanding of cell-cell communication during embryonic kidney development. It highlights that classical pathway-centered models (GDNF/RET, WNT, FGF, BMP, Notch, Hedgehog, VEGF, PDGF) are insufficient to explain the complexity of signaling among ureteric epithelium, nephron progenitors, stroma, endothelium, and differentiating nephrons, and argues that spatially resolved, cell-type-specific interaction maps provide a more complete picture.

papers.title: Pan-Cancer Metabolic Landscapes: A Multiomics View.
papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming fuels cancer progression, but whether common metabolic patterns exist across diverse malignancies remains incompletely understood. To address this, we integrated large-scale proteomic, transcriptomic [The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)], and spatial transcriptomic (Spatial Meta-Transcriptome Database) data sets comprising 3226 samples across 24 human cancer types. Utilizing a highly controlled, predominantly patient-matched design to minimize background noise, we characterized the pan-cancer metabolic landscape via reaction-level functional task scoring, pathway enrichment,
papers.summary: This study integrated proteomic, transcriptomic, and spatial transcriptomic data from 3,226 samples across 24 cancer types to map metabolic reprogramming patterns shared across malignancies. Using reaction-level functional scoring and pathway enrichment, the authors identified common metabolic features in the pan-cancer landscape. The work provides a multiomics resource for understanding conserved metabolic vulnerabilities across diverse cancers.

papers.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
papers.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se
papers.summary: The authors present CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq data into cell-type composition and cell-type-specific expression, then uses this to infer drug sensitivity from bulk samples. This addresses the problem that bulk measurements average over heterogeneous cell mixtures, obscuring cell-specific signals relevant to drug response. The approach maps single-cell transcriptomes to bulk data to enable computational drug-sensitivity prediction.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from public repositories to characterize cell adhesion-related gene expression patterns in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors identify gene signatures linked to inflammatory infiltration and blood-brain barrier disruption, proposing these as potential therapeutic targets. The work is largely descriptive and based on reanalysis of existing datasets without experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to characterize the ovarian cancer microenvironment, identifying chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets as key drivers of poor clinical outcomes. The findings suggest that these inflammatory and fibroblast populations, which persist after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, contribute to treatment resistance and adverse prognosis.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors present Pasta, a transcriptomic aging clock trained with a novel 'age-shift' learning framework that predicts relative biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq and microarray data. Predictions aligned with senescence and stem-like states, and the clock was used to map chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation. This provides a versatile, platform-independent tool for studying aging biology.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review argues that spatial transcriptomics, while valuable for understanding tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment organization, captures only gene expression and misses the epigenetic regulatory programs that shape cancer within intact tissue architecture. The authors make the case for developing and applying spatially resolved epigenomic technologies to study cancer biology in its native spatial context.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue for immunohistochemistry, allowing them to map the development of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye on a single timeline. They combined this with re-analysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data to build a unified developmental atlas of ocular pigmented tissues. This provides a practical methodological advance and a reference resource for studying eye development.

papers.title: Condition-Associated Pattern Extraction and Recovery From Multi-Condition Single-Cell RNA-seq Data With CAPER.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in multi-condition single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is the disentanglement of true biological signals from unwanted variations in complex experimental designs. Current statistical and machine learning-based methods struggle with this task, often providing only visualizable embeddings, over-correcting and discarding biological signal, or failing to resolve cell-type-specific responses. Here, we present CAPER, a matrix factorization framework that explicitly disentangles shared biological states from condition-specific variations. CAPER directly outputs an
papers.summary: CAPER is a new matrix factorization framework for multi-condition single-cell RNA-seq data that separates shared biological states from condition-specific variation, avoiding the over-correction and signal loss seen in existing methods. It directly outputs interpretable condition-associated expression patterns and resolves cell-type-specific responses, rather than only producing visual embeddings.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarked 465 computational pipelines (combinations of normalization methods and clustering algorithms) across three cancer scRNA-seq datasets totaling over 434,000 cells. The authors introduce a Biological Discordance Score to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts across pipelines, and find that normalization choice affects biological interpretation more strongly than clustering algorithm choice. The work highlights that seemingly technical preprocessing decisions can materially change downstream biological conclusions in cancer single-cell studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This study investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, proposing that gut microbes and their metabolites migrate to intervertebral discs and contribute to disc degeneration (IVDD), a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify key microbial species and molecular mechanisms mediating this cross-kingdom migration, though the abstract does not report specific findings.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis of high-grade serous ovarian cancers reveals heterogeneity and distinct immunological patterns based upon clinico-genomic status.
papers.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by remarkable intratumoral heterogeneity and variable tissue architectures, dictating differential therapeutic responses. Although BRCA1/2 mutations correlate with improved responses to DNA-damaging agents, how BRCA genotype shapes the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated whole exome sequencing, total RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to profile a cohort of BRCA-mutated (BRCA-MT) and non-BRCA-mutated (BRCA-WT) HGSOC tumors. While bulk transcriptomics highlighted global phenot
papers.summary: This study integrates whole-exome sequencing, bulk RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to characterize how BRCA mutation status shapes the tumor immune microenvironment in high-grade serous ovarian cancer. The authors find substantial intratumoral heterogeneity and distinct immunological patterns between BRCA-mutated and BRCA-wildtype tumors, suggesting that clinico-genomic status influences immune contexture. These multi-omic profiles may help explain differential therapeutic responses and inform immunotherapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analysis Identifies Novel Immune-Associated Biomarkers of Anti-PD1 Response in Metastatic Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Resistance to anti-PD1 therapy remains a major challenge in metastatic melanoma, despite long-term benefit in some patients. Since a functional dendritic cell (DC)-CD8+ T cell axis is essential for anti-PD1 response, biomarkers associated with this axis may help characterize underexplored immune states linked to resistance. Here, we further characterized poor survival predictor (PSP) biomarkers previously negatively correlated with DC-CD8+ T cell axis in melanoma, evaluating their associations with anti-PD1 response, immune infiltration, and transcriptional and proteomic signatures. Pre-treatm
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of pre-treatment metastatic melanoma samples to characterize 'poor survival predictor' (PSP) biomarkers previously linked to a disrupted dendritic cell–CD8+ T cell axis. The authors show these PSP biomarkers associate with anti-PD1 response, immune infiltration patterns, and distinct transcriptional/proteomic signatures, nominating them as candidate biomarkers of immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Bulk and single-cell analysis of FAM72D reveals its prognostic and functional relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Family with sequence similarity 72 member D (FAM72D) has been implicated in proliferative programs in several malignancies, but its clinical significance, cellular distribution and underlying biological programs in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain insufficiently characterized. FAM72D expression and its clinical relevance were evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas-liver hepatocellular carcinoma (TCGA-LIHC) cohort and three independent GEO cohorts. Cox regression, patient-level bootstrap validation, calibration analysis and decision curve analysis were used to assess its prognostic contri
papers.summary: This study analyzes FAM72D expression in hepatocellular carcinoma using TCGA and three independent GEO cohorts, showing that higher FAM72D levels are associated with worse patient prognosis. Bulk and single-cell analyses suggest FAM72D marks proliferative tumor programs and has potential as a prognostic biomarker in HCC.

papers.title: Patient classification using single-cell RNA-sequencing data with deep learning convolutional neural networks.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables gene expression profiling at the resolution of individual cells, revealing cellular heterogeneity that is obscured in bulk RNA-seq. While this offers a powerful lens to study disease-specific changes, leveraging scRNA-seq data for patient phenotype classification remains challenging due to limited sample numbers, cell count variability, high dimensionality, and dependence on cell-type annotations. Existing tools attempt to address these issues using probabilistic models or attention mechanisms, but face limitations in scalability, interpretability
papers.summary: This paper introduces a deep learning convolutional neural network approach for classifying patient phenotypes directly from single-cell RNA-sequencing data. The method aims to overcome common challenges such as limited sample sizes, variable cell counts, high dimensionality, and reliance on cell-type annotations. It offers a potentially more scalable and interpretable alternative to existing probabilistic or attention-based tools.

papers.title: FDX1 is associated with CALR abundance and JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are driven by constitutive cytokine-receptor signaling, yet the metabolic programs associated with driver genotype and inflammatory remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study investigates the metabolic enzyme FDX1 in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), finding that its expression is associated with calreticulin (CALR) abundance and with JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling. The work links a metabolic factor to driver-genotype-associated inflammatory remodeling in MPNs, suggesting FDX1 as a potential node connecting metabolism and cytokine signaling.

papers.title: Development and External Validation of an M2 Macrophage-Related Prognostic Signature in Breast Cancer Using Multi-Omics Data and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), particularly the M2-like phenotype, are central regulators of breast cancer progression; however, clinically applicable models capturing their functional heterogeneity and biological mechanisms remain limited.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates a prognostic signature for breast cancer based on M2 macrophage-related genes, using multi-omics data and machine learning. The model aims to capture the functional heterogeneity of tumor-associated macrophages and link it to patient outcomes. External validation supports its potential clinical applicability as a prognostic tool.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Rora-Associated Aberrant Granulosa Cell Differentiation in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by follicular developmental arrest, yet the molecular basis underlying impaired granulosa cell (GC) differentiation remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics to profile granulosa cells in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), revealing aberrant differentiation states associated with the transcription factor Rora. The findings suggest that disrupted Rora-associated granulosa cell maturation contributes to the follicular developmental arrest characteristic of PCOS.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics combined with machine learning to unravel the heterogeneity of cholangiocarcinoma and the WFDC3-mediated prognostic regulatory mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) exhibits substantial cellular heterogeneity and a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), contributing to poor clinical outcomes. Effective prognostic biomarkers and a deeper understanding of the cellular ecosystems associated with high-risk disease remain urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial multi-omics with machine learning to characterize cellular heterogeneity and the tumor microenvironment in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The authors identify WFDC3 as a key gene linked to prognostic regulatory mechanisms, proposing it as a potential biomarker for stratifying high-risk disease.

papers.title: Study on tumor ecology and precision medicine strategy of oral squamous cell carcinoma based on multi-omics cell atlas.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is characterized by inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity, which complicates patient stratification and treatment. Although single-cell studies have improved the resolution of the OSCC microenvironment, the relationships among cellular states, spatial organization, immune-repertoire dynamics, and patient-level ecosystem patterns remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study constructs a multi-omics single-cell atlas of oral squamous cell carcinoma to characterize tumor heterogeneity across cellular states, spatial organization, and immune-repertoire dynamics. The authors use these ecosystem-level patterns to propose a framework for patient stratification and precision medicine strategies in OSCC.

papers.title: Histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomic analysis identifies an ECM-associated stromal pattern in lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma with complementary proteomic and functional analyses.
papers.abstract: Lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) is a rare but locally aggressive malignancy characterized by perineural invasion, recurrence, and limited systemic treatment options. Although extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of tumor progression, its spatial organization and functional relevance in LGACC remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study uses histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomics on lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma, a rare and aggressive eye tumor, to map gene expression within its tissue architecture. The authors identify a distinct stromal pattern associated with extracellular matrix remodeling and support it with complementary proteomic and functional experiments. The work suggests ECM-associated stromal programs may contribute to LGACC progression and could represent candidate therapeutic targets.

papers.title: HEXB as a Candidate Target Gene in Keloid Radiotherapy: Based on Multi-Omics Analysis and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a common and treatment-refractory conditions in plastic surgery and dermatology. Although radiotherapy for keloid has attracted increasing attention in recent years, its mechanism at the genetic level remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the relationship between radiation-related genes (RRGs) and keloid through an integrated multi-omics and machine learning framework, and to explore potential therapeutic agents targeting the identified key gene.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data, machine learning, and Mendelian randomization to identify HEXB as a candidate gene linking radiation-related pathways to keloid formation. The authors propose HEXB as a potential therapeutic target for keloid radiotherapy, though the finding is based on computational prioritization rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Mapping the hepatic neural niche: from three-dimensional innervation architecture to periportal interoception and human translation.
papers.abstract: The liver has traditionally been viewed as an organ regulated by circulating hormones and long-range autonomic reflexes, with its intrahepatic neural architecture receiving comparatively little systematic attention. However, recent advances in tissue clearing, three-dimensional (3D) volumetric imaging, neural tracing, and spatial omics are reshaping this view. Here we synthesize emerging evidence that the hepatic nervous system is organized around spatially defined neurovascular-cellular niches, and propose the periportal region as a dominant anatomical site for interoceptive integration, whil
papers.summary: This review synthesizes emerging evidence that the liver contains a spatially organized neural architecture centered on neurovascular-cellular niches, with the periportal region proposed as a key site for interoceptive integration. It highlights how tissue clearing, 3D volumetric imaging, neural tracing, and spatial omics are reshaping the traditional view of the liver as regulated mainly by circulating hormones and long-range autonomic reflexes.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing combined with artificial intelligence to uncover immunotherapy biomarkers and decipher drug resistance mechanisms in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma represents the most aggressive primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system, characterized by extensive intratumoral heterogeneity, profound immunosuppression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Although immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, its clinical efficacy in GBM remains limited, largely due to the complexity of the tumor ecosystem and the lack of validated predictive biomarkers. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational approaches have provi
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and AI-based computational methods can be combined to identify immunotherapy biomarkers and understand drug resistance in glioblastoma. It highlights that GBM's intratumoral heterogeneity and immunosuppressive microenvironment limit immunotherapy efficacy, and argues these technologies can help decode the tumor ecosystem and guide more personalized treatment strategies.

papers.title: From density to spatial function: spatial multi-omics, composite biomarker design, and therapeutic engineering of tertiary lymphoid structures in solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) have emerged as clinically relevant immune niches associated with improved survival and enhanced response to immune checkpoint inhibitors across multiple solid tumors. However, translational evaluation remains dominated by density-based scoring, which inadequately captures the functional heterogeneity of histologically similar lymphoid aggregates. This review synthesizes recent advances in spatial biology that support a shift from counting TLSs to interpreting them as spatially organized immune microenvironmental units embedded within local tumor ecosystems.
papers.summary: This review argues that simply counting tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in tumors is insufficient, because histologically similar aggregates can differ functionally. It synthesizes spatial multi-omics approaches that characterize TLSs as organized immune microenvironmental units, and discusses using these to design composite biomarkers and engineer TLS-targeted therapies. The key message is a shift from density-based scoring to spatially resolved functional interpretation of TLSs in solid tumors.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis reveals a membrane tension signature associated with tumor-stroma crosstalk in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Dysregulated membrane tension (MT) drives tumor cell migration, invasion, and immune evasion, yet the prognostic value of MT-related genes (MTRGs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to define a membrane tension-related gene signature in hepatocellular carcinoma and links it to tumor-stroma crosstalk. The authors propose that this signature has prognostic value and reflects immune and stromal interactions in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: An entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification and molecular characterization in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Entosis is an actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell process that may culminate in lysosome-mediated entotic cell death and is implicated in tumor evolution. Its clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study constructs a prognostic index for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to entosis, a cell-in-cell process implicated in tumor evolution. The index stratifies patients by survival and is linked to molecular characterization, suggesting entosis-related signatures may have clinical utility in LUAD.
